query: Consider the following context: High entropy alloys have excellent wear resistance, so they have great application prospects in the fields of wear resistance and surface protection. In that context, which material can be used for adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A high entropy alloy (HEA) coating, specifically a CrMnFeCoNi alloy, can be used to adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, enhancing its wear resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Cu matrix in its pure, annealed state
generation.intervention: Deposition of a CrMnFeCoNi high entropy alloy coating using magnetron sputtering with a thickness of 5 micrometers
generation.conditions: Deposition temperature of 300°C, working pressure of 0.5 Pa, and a substrate bias voltage of -50 V
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a strong metallurgical bond between the Cu matrix and the HEA coating, facilitated by interdiffusion and the creation of a gradient interface
generation.mechanism: The high entropy alloy coating provides a hard, wear-resistant surface layer, while the Cu matrix offers a ductile, toughness-enhancing substrate, thus combining the benefits of both materials
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% increase in wear resistance compared to the uncoated Cu matrix, as measured by a reduction in wear volume loss (in mm³) under a load of 10 N and a sliding distance of 1000 m
generation.boundary: A minimum of 20% increase in wear resistance to confirm the effectiveness of the HEA coating
generation.uncertainty: The actual wear resistance improvement may vary depending on the specific deposition conditions, coating thickness, and testing parameters, as well as potential interfacial reactions between the Cu matrix and the HEA coating

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test using a ball-on-disk tribometer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear volume loss of the HEA-coated Cu matrix is not at least 20% lower than that of the uncoated Cu matrix, the hypothesis is falsified, with a threshold of p < 0.05
